sections.label: Integrated Shield Plan rider questions
sections.summary: Questions asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health about new Integrated Shield Plan rider requirements, premiums, regulation and support measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health regarding the new Integrated Shield Plan rider requirements (a) whether there will be an absolute cap on patients' out-of-pocket costs; (b) whether insurers can retain older policies with higher coverage; and (c) what measures will be implemented to prevent insurers from unilaterally reducing coverage for ageing policyholders on existing plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health in view of the Ministry’s move to curb rising healthcare insurance premiums by April 2026, how will families facing hefty medical bills be supported if their out-of-pocket expenses for co-payments become unaffordable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health regarding the new Integrated Shield Plan rider (a) whether the policy design anticipates that policyholders will continue to access private healthcare despite higher cost-sharing; (b) if so, what is the policy basis; and (c) what contingency measures have been developed to support restructured hospitals should there be increased patient volume due to shifts from private to public healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health given that the Monetary Authority of Singapore primarily regulates solvency, whether the Ministry intends to establish a dual-regulation framework to oversee the (i) healthcare outcomes (ii) panel selection criteria and (iii) loss-ratio efficiency of private insurers to ensure they align with national health goals.

sections.label: Private and public split 2010
sections.summary: In 2010, the split between private and public was 15:85.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In 2010, the split between private and public was 15:85.

sections.label: IP premium growth and cancellations
sections.summary: IP premiums for private hospital grew about 17% annually for three years, and about 100,000 policyholders yearly cancel or downgrade IP rider policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: IP premiums for private hospital have been growing at an average rate of 17% annually for the past three years – it is double that of IP premiums and even higher compared to MediShield Life premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Hence, every year, about 100,000 policyholders cancel or downgrade their IP rider policies.

sections.label: Lower IP rider premiums
sections.summary: Under the new design, IP rider premiums should be on average 30% lower than existing policies with maximum coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: First, IP rider premiums under the new design should be lower, on average 30% lower, compared to existing policies with maximum coverage.

sections.label: MOH and MAS oversight
sections.summary: MOH and MAS work closely together in regulatory oversight of IP insurers to protect policyholders' interests and ensure products are sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On Mr Kenneth Tiong’s question relating to the regulation of IP insurers, the Ministry of Health (MOH) and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) work closely together in exercising regulatory oversight of IP insurers, to ensure that policyholders’ interests are protected and the products are sustainable.

sections.label: IP requirements and market intervention
sections.summary: Requirements cover key IP and rider parameters like co-payment and deductible, with intervention only for serious market failure, as in tightening IP rider design.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Instead, we set requirements pertaining to the key parameters of IPs and riders, such as co-payment and deductible requirements, to ensure that the schemes are sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We only step in when we see a serious market failure emerging, which is why we have intervened in this case, to tighten the design of IP riders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Doctor panels are an example of cost-management measures put in place by the market, by insurers in response to rising private healthcare bills and claims.

sections.label: New rider design co-payment
sections.summary: New riders are given a different design with more co-payment to instil discipline in healthcare supply and demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: To redress this, for new riders, we are making the design different, a bit more co-payment, instil discipline in both the supply and demand for healthcare; then, I think we are much more likely to have a more sustainable position.

sections.label: Savings on new rider premiums
sections.summary: Those who choose the new rider design save on average 30% on premiums every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If they choose the new rider design, they save, on average, 30% on premiums every year.

sections.label: Continuity of care and subsidised healthcare
sections.summary: Continuity of care is a key question, and public subsidised healthcare always exists for those who give up their IP rider.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But if I were to suss out what are the key questions, one is, you want to have continuity of care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, be assured, even if they find that, today, they cannot afford their IP rider anymore, because it is getting expensive and they give it up, there is always public subsidised healthcare.

sections.label: People changing and calculations
sections.summary: More people calculate that it is not worth it, and 100,000 every year are changing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And more and more people do their calculations and find that it is not worth it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And as it is, 100,000 every year are changing.

sections.label: MAS and MOH action on IP riders
sections.summary: The IP rider has become a problem, and MAS and MOH will work together to ensure insurers operate ethically and viably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The IP rider has become a problem and we are taking action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Between MAS and MOH, I think we have plenty of levers and we will work together to make sure that insurers are operating in a way that is ethical, that is viable but at the same time in the interest of patients and the people we serve.

sections.label: Regulation of clinical effectiveness and safety
sections.summary: Regulation covers clinical effectiveness, safety, and key parameters that make the system sustainable without market failure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Where we regulate is clinical effectiveness, safety, and key parameters that are sensible and make the system sustainable, and there is no market failure.
